systems.title: Computers, phones, accounts, Wi‑Fi, and everyday tech problems.
systems.problem: The regular problems people run into: slow devices, confusing apps, account issues, printers, updates, backups, cleanup, and setup.
systems.work: I troubleshoot the device, the software, the account, and the network instead of blaming the first thing I see. I explain what happened and what to do next.

systems.title: Help across Windows, macOS, Linux, iPhone, Android, and odd setups.
systems.problem: Not every job lives on one platform. Families, small teams, and personal setups usually have a mix of devices that all need to work together.
systems.work: I move between operating systems, transfer data, clean up problems, install software, fix settings, recover access, and learn unfamiliar systems when the job calls for it.

systems.title: Linux servers, self-hosted apps, storage, backups, and remote access.
systems.problem: I run real services for media, photos, game servers, automation, files, dashboards, and everyday tools. They need to stay organized and recoverable.
systems.work: I handle Docker Compose stacks, storage paths, DNS, tunnels, private networking, firewalls, monitoring, updates, moves between machines, and backup/recovery checks.

systems.title: Websites, dashboards, scripts, and little tools that solve real problems.
systems.problem: Sometimes the missing piece is not a big app. It is a cleaner homepage, a dashboard, a status page, a script, or a workflow that saves repeated manual work.
systems.work: I build React pages, small utilities, service dashboards, automation scripts, API integrations, and practical admin tools that can improve over time.

systems.title: AI agents and automations that do useful work, not just chat.
systems.problem: I use AI for hands-on help: server checks, Discord/iMessage workflows, scheduled jobs, research, and passing specialized problems to the right tools.
systems.work: I operate Hermes agents, connect tools, schedule checks, route model providers, keep permissions separated, and test whether an automation actually did the job.

systems.title: Consoles, controllers, older devices, cleaning, parts, and testing.
systems.problem: I like giving hardware a fair chance before it gets thrown away. A lot of devices need diagnosis, cleaning, parts, software recovery, or an honest “not worth it” call.
systems.work: I disassemble carefully, inspect, clean, swap parts, prepare storage, recover software when possible, test the result, and explain the risk before parts get ordered.

experience.place: Renew Range Holdings · CareFree Living Center
experience.description: I maintain computers, internet service, and connected devices. I handle support requests, hardware problems, software troubleshooting, upgrades, and the day-to-day work that keeps technology out of everyone else’s way.
Customer service in a busy store taught me how to listen, explain things clearly, stay organized, and solve the problem in front of me without making the customer feel rushed.
I handled opening and closing, inventory, equipment, deliveries, cleaning, employee training, customer issues, and whatever else needed attention that day.
I supported customers and helped keep front-line store operations organized and dependable.
I spoke with students about Jewish practices, holidays, daily life, Israel, and culture. It pushed me to get comfortable speaking to unfamiliar groups and answering honest questions.

fieldNotes: I move between Linux, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and oddball setups without treating any one platform like the only answer.
I can explain the problem to a person, then go back to the terminal, workbench, router, or config file and actually fix it.
When I hit something new, I read the docs, test safely, verify the result, and keep notes so the fix becomes part of my toolkit.
I like owning the whole chain: the device, the network, the service, the user experience, and the follow-through after it ships.
resumeHighlights: Hands-on IT support for computers, internet service, connected devices, upgrades, and troubleshooting.
Linux homelab operator running real services, remote access, storage, backups, firewalls, and monitoring.
AI automation builder using agents, scheduled jobs, Discord/iMessage gateways, and practical tool integrations.
Repair-minded technician comfortable with consoles, controllers, PCs, Macs, phones, and older hardware.
